cards.text: Le RAG récupère des passages pertinents dans vos documents et les donne au modèle avec la question, pour que les réponses viennent de vos sources plutôt que de la mémoire du modèle.

deep.x: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), named in a 2020 Facebook AI paper, combines a search step with generation. Instead of answering from memory, the model answers from retrieved passages placed in its context.
Why it works
Models are good at reading and synthesising text in front of them, and much less reliable at recalling specific facts from training. RAG plays to their strength.
Typical enterprise uses
Agentic RAG
Newer systems let the model decide when and what to search, run several searches, read results and search again, handling questions that need multiple steps.
RAG is probably the most common architecture behind enterprise "chat with your documents" tools.

cards.title: Pourquoi ne pas simplement affiner ?
cards.text: L'affinage enseigne un style et un comportement, mais c'est une mauvaise façon d'ajouter des faits qui changent. Le RAG se met à jour instantanément quand les documents changent et peut citer ses sources.

deep.x: Fine-tuning changes model weights through training; RAG changes what the model sees at question time. They solve different problems.
Facts in weights are fragile
Fine-tuning on documents doesn't reliably make a model recall exact facts, and it can increase hallucination of plausible-sounding details. Updating facts means retraining.
Combining both

items.b: what to say: facts and sources
how to say it: format, tone, domain style

deep.x: Decision guide

items: Need consistent format or tone? Fine-tune or prompt
Narrow repetitive task at scale? Consider fine-tuning a small model

deep.x: Start with prompting plus RAG; fine-tune only when evaluations show a clear gap.

cards.title: La chaîne d'ingestion
cards.text: Les documents sont chargés, nettoyés, découpés en segments, enrichis de métadonnées (date, propriétaire, type), vectorisés et indexés.

deep.x: Ingestion turns raw documents into a searchable index. Quality here determines everything downstream.
Sources
Metadata that helps
Parsing challenges
Complex PDFs, scanned documents, tables, headers and footers often break naive text extraction. Specialised document-parsing tools and vision-language models help preserve structure.
A surprising amount of RAG effort goes into deciding which documents should be included at all: outdated drafts can poison answers.

cards.title: Tout dépend de la qualité de récupération
cards.text: Si la récupération rate le bon passage, le modèle ne peut pas bien répondre. La plupart des améliorations du RAG viennent d'un meilleur découpage, de la recherche hybride, des filtres de métadonnées et du re-classement.

deep.x: The model can only answer from what's retrieved. If the right passage isn't in the top results, even the best model will fail or guess.
Improvement levers
Query rewriting
Users ask vague or conversational questions ("what about the other one?"). Rewriting the query into a standalone, specific search, or generating several variations, improves retrieval.
Measure retrieval separately

items.b: was the right passage in the top k?
how many retrieved passages were relevant?

deep.x: When a RAG answer is wrong, check retrieval first: was the right text even found?

cards.title: Citations

items.r: réponse avec passages cités
dire que ce n'est pas dans les documents

cards.text: Demander au modèle de citer le passage qui étaye chaque affirmation permet aux utilisateurs de vérifier les réponses et renforce la confiance. Une réponse sans appui doit dire « Je ne sais pas ».

deep.x: Citations link each claim to its source passage, letting users verify answers and building trust. They also discourage the model from inventing information.

items.r: "The demurrage rate is $18,000 per day [Contract 4471, clause 12.3, p. 8]"

deep.x: Implementation

items: Instruct the model to cite after each claim
Link citations to document and page
Check cited passages actually support claims

deep.x: Faithfulness checks
Automated checks can verify that cited passages contain the claimed information, flagging unsupported statements.

steps: Check each claim against its passage

deep.x: Saying "I don't know"
Instruct the system to say when the documents don't contain the answer, rather than filling gaps from memory. Users trust a system more when it admits limits.

items: answer with citations, or "not found in the documents"

deep.x: Some products show the exact highlighted sentence in the original document when you click a citation.

cards.title: Contrôle d'accès
cards.text: Dans une entreprise, le RAG doit respecter les permissions : les utilisateurs ne doivent récupérer que les documents qu'ils ont le droit de voir. Filtrez selon les droits de l'utilisateur au moment de la récupération.

deep.x: Enterprise RAG must enforce the same permissions as the source systems. Otherwise, a chatbot could reveal salaries, legal cases or board papers to anyone who asks.
Approaches
Common mistakes

x: Indexing all documents with a service account that sees everything
Permissions changing in the source but not in the index
Answers combining information from documents with different access levels

deep.x: Audit
Log who asked what and which documents were retrieved, to investigate incidents and demonstrate compliance.
"Oversharing" through AI search is one of the top enterprise concerns; fix permissions in sources before indexing.

cards.title: Données structurées
cards.text: Pour les chiffres des bases de données (ventes, stocks), mieux vaut laisser le modèle écrire une requête (SQL) ou appeler une API que vectoriser des tableaux comme du texte.

deep.x: Numbers in databases, like sales, stock, positions and prices, are better queried than embedded. Converting tables to text chunks loses structure and makes calculations unreliable.
Text-to-SQL
The model translates a question into SQL using the database schema, runs it, and explains the results.

steps: "Total wheat shipped to Egypt in Q3?"

deep.x: Making it reliable

items: Use curated views or a semantic layer

deep.x: Combining sources
Real questions often mix both: "Which contracts with late deliveries have penalty clauses?" needs database records and document clauses. Agentic systems can query both and combine results.
A semantic layer that defines business terms ("net margin", "active customer") consistently makes text-to-SQL much more accurate.

cards.title: Évaluer un RAG
cards.text: Mesurez la récupération (a-t-on trouvé les bons passages ?) et la génération (la réponse est-elle correcte, complète et fidèle aux sources ?). Constituez un jeu de test de vraies questions aux réponses connues.

deep.x: RAG has two components to evaluate: retrieval and generation. Both can fail independently.

items.b: is the answer supported by the passages?

deep.x: Building a test set

steps: Have experts write correct answers and sources

deep.x: Tools
Frameworks such as RAGAS and others automate many metrics using LLM judges, but calibrate them against expert review.
Unanswerable questions
Include questions whose answers aren't in the documents. A good system says so instead of inventing an answer.
Evaluate continuously: document collections and user questions change over time.

cards.title: Questions-réponses sur les contrats
cards.text: Un trader demande : « Quel est le taux de surestaries du contrat 4471 ? » Le RAG récupère la clause pertinente, le modèle répond « 18 000 $ par jour, clause 12,3 » et renvoie vers la page.

deep.x: Commodity contracts contain terms that traders, operators and finance teams constantly need: laytime, demurrage, quality specifications, payment terms, force majeure. RAG makes them searchable in plain language.

steps: Answer with citation and page link

deep.x: Extraction plus Q&A
Many systems combine two approaches: extract key terms into structured fields for dashboards and checks, and use RAG for ad-hoc questions.
Fields often extracted
Accuracy safeguards

x: Human review for low-confidence or high-value fields

deep.x: Comparing a counterparty's draft against standard terms and highlighting deviations is a common high-value use for legal and trading teams.

cards.title: Échecs courants
cards.text: Problèmes typiques : documents périmés, versions en double, tableaux cassés par l'analyse des PDF, questions nécessitant des informations de nombreux documents, et questions d'utilisateur vagues.

deep.x: Most RAG problems come from data and retrieval, not the language model.
Typical symptoms
Fixes
Questions RAG struggles with
"Summarise all contracts with clause X" or "which supplier had most delays?" need aggregation across many documents; better handled with extraction into structured data plus queries.
Garbage in, garbage out applies doubly to RAG: clean, current documents matter more than model choice.

quiz.q: Qu'ajoute le RAG à un prompt ?
options: Des passages pertinents extraits de vos documents
quiz.explain: Il ancre les réponses dans vos sources.

quiz.q: Les faits qui changent souvent sont mieux gérés par…
quiz.explain: Le RAG se met à jour instantanément quand les documents changent.

quiz.q: Pourquoi un RAG d'entreprise doit-il vérifier les permissions ?
options: Pour que les utilisateurs ne voient que les documents auxquels ils ont accès
quiz.explain: La sécurité doit être appliquée dès la récupération.

lessons.title: Adapter les modèles
lessons.summary: Affinage, LoRA et distillation.

cards.title: Quand affiner
cards.text: L'affinage poursuit l'entraînement d'un modèle sur vos exemples pour changer son comportement : un format constant, un style maison, une tâche de classification étroite. Essayez d'abord le prompting et le RAG ; affinez quand ils ne suffisent pas.

deep.x: Fine-tuning continues training a pre-trained model on your examples. It's powerful but adds cost, maintenance and risk. Use it when cheaper methods fall short.
Good reasons to fine-tune

items: Shorter prompts to cut cost and latency
Making a small model match a large one on one task

deep.x: Poor reasons

x: Fixing problems that clearer prompts would solve
Before having an evaluation set to measure improvement

items: fine-tuning if evals show a gap

deep.x: The ladder: prompt → add examples → add retrieval → fine-tune → train from scratch (almost never).

cards.title: Ce qu'il vous faut

items: Un jeu de test mis de côté

cards.text: De quelques centaines à quelques milliers d'exemples de qualité d'entrée et de sortie idéale. La qualité compte bien plus que la quantité : des exemples incohérents enseignent un comportement incohérent.

deep.x: Fine-tuning needs well-curated training examples, a held-out evaluation set and clear success criteria.

items.b: hundreds to thousands of input–output pairs

deep.x: Data quality
Examples must be consistent: if three annotators format outputs differently, the model learns inconsistency. Write guidelines and review samples.
Data sources

x: Outputs from a stronger model, reviewed by humans

deep.x: Privacy
Training data may include personal or confidential information; check legal basis, anonymise where possible and confirm where training happens.
Fine-tuned models can memorise and repeat training examples, so don't include secrets you wouldn't want the model to output.

cards.title: Affinage complet ou LoRA
cards.text: L'affinage complet met à jour tous les poids : c'est coûteux. LoRA (adaptation de bas rang) gèle le modèle et entraîne de petites matrices additionnelles, avec une infime fraction de la mémoire et de petits fichiers d'adaptateur.

deep.x: Full fine-tuning updates all weights and needs memory for weights, gradients and optimiser states, several times the model size. LoRA (2021) freezes the original weights and learns small low-rank matrices added to certain layers.
How small?
QLoRA
QLoRA (2023) combines 4-bit quantisation of the base model with LoRA adapters, letting people fine-tune large models on a single GPU.

steps: Load with base model to use

deep.x: Multiple adapters
One base model can serve many LoRA adapters, one per task or customer, switching quickly. This makes customisation cheap at scale.
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning made customising open models accessible to small teams.

cards.title: Distillation
cards.text: Un grand modèle « enseignant » génère des réponses ; un modèle « élève » plus petit est entraîné à les imiter. L'élève est moins cher et plus rapide, souvent presque aussi bon sur la tâche visée.

deep.x: Distillation transfers capability from a large teacher to a smaller student. For language models, this often means the teacher generates high-quality answers or reasoning traces for many prompts, and the student is fine-tuned on them.
Why

items.b: small models cost far less per request
can run on-premise or on devices

deep.x: Results
Distilled models can match much larger models on narrow tasks, though they usually lose some general ability.
Terms of service
Some model providers restrict using their outputs to train competing models; check licences before distilling.
DeepSeek released smaller models distilled from its R1 reasoning model in 2025, showing reasoning skills can transfer to compact models.

cards.title: Ajustement par préférences
cards.text: Au lieu de réponses uniques et correctes, vous pouvez entraîner sur des paires de réponses meilleure et moins bonne (par exemple avec le DPO), ce qui façonne le ton et l'utilité.

deep.x: Preference tuning trains on comparisons: for a prompt, a preferred response and a rejected one. It shapes subtle qualities like tone, helpfulness and conciseness that are hard to specify with single "correct" answers.

steps: Train model to favour preferred style

deep.x: DPO
Direct Preference Optimisation (2023) trains directly on preference pairs without a separate reward model or reinforcement learning loop, making preference tuning simpler and more stable.
Business uses
Collecting preferences
Preferences can come from user feedback (thumbs up/down, edits), expert comparisons or AI judges guided by guidelines.
Edits users make to AI drafts are a rich source of preference data.

cards.title: Oubli catastrophique

items.w: entraîner fort sur une seule tâche
items.r: mêler des exemples généraux et utiliser LoRA

cards.text: Un affinage trop poussé sur une tâche étroite peut rendre un modèle moins bon sur d'autres choses. Des taux d'apprentissage plus bas, LoRA et le mélange de données générales aident.

deep.x: When fine-tuning hard on narrow data, neural networks can overwrite general abilities learned earlier: catastrophic forgetting. A model tuned on invoices might become worse at general reasoning or safety behaviour.

items.w: "Train longer on our data = better model"
items.r: Over-training can erase general skills and safety behaviour

deep.x: Mitigations
Safety erosion
Research in 2023 found that fine-tuning on even small datasets could weaken a model's safety training, sometimes unintentionally. Re-test safety after fine-tuning.
Evaluate broadly
Keep a general evaluation set alongside your task set to detect regressions.
LoRA's frozen base weights reduce forgetting because the original knowledge isn't overwritten.

cards.title: Modèles de domaine

items: plus facile à mettre à jour

cards.text: Certaines organisations adaptent des modèles à un domaine comme le droit, la médecine ou la finance, avec un vocabulaire et des documents spécialisés. Souvent, de bons modèles généraux associés au RAG font aussi bien, voire mieux.

deep.x: Domain-specific models are trained or adapted on specialised text: medicine, law, finance, chemistry. BloombergGPT (2023), trained partly on financial data, is a well-known example.
The general-model surprise
Evaluations showed that subsequent general models often matched or beat earlier domain-specific models on domain tasks, because general capability improved so quickly.
When domain adaptation helps

items: Languages or formats rare on the web

deep.x: Middle path
Continued pre-training on domain text, then instruction tuning, can boost a mid-sized open model, but requires significant data and compute.
For most companies, the best "domain model" is a strong general model with good retrieval and prompts.

cards.title: Héberger des modèles affinés
cards.text: Les fournisseurs cloud permettent d'affiner et d'héberger certains modèles via une API. Les modèles ouverts peuvent être affinés et servis sur vos propres GPU.

deep.x: Fine-tuned models need serving infrastructure: GPU capacity, scaling, monitoring and version management.

items.b: fine-tune via API, provider serves it
Azure, AWS, Google host open and proprietary models
your GPUs with vLLM or similar
pay per use for LoRA models

deep.x: Costs
Self-hosting has fixed GPU costs; it's economical only with steady, high volume. Provider-hosted fine-tunes often cost more per token than base models.
Operations

items: Plan updates when base models change

deep.x: Serving engines like vLLM use techniques such as paged attention to serve many users efficiently on the same GPUs.

cards.title: Mesurer le gain
cards.text: Comparez le modèle affiné au modèle de base avec un bon prompt, sur le même jeu de test. Si l'amélioration est faible, le surcoût et la maintenance ne valent peut-être pas la peine.

deep.x: Every fine-tune should be justified by evaluation against strong baselines on the same test set.
Total cost of ownership
Include data preparation, training runs, hosting, monitoring, retraining and staff time. A 4-point gain may or may not justify these.
Statistical confidence
Small test sets produce noisy estimates. With 100 examples, a few points' difference may be chance; use larger sets or confidence intervals.
If a better prompt gets you most of the way, keep the prompt.

cards.title: Rester à jour
cards.text: De nouveaux modèles de base arrivent souvent. Un affinage du modèle de l'an dernier peut être battu par le modèle de cette année avec un simple prompt. Gardez vos données d'entraînement et vos évaluations prêtes à être relancées.

deep.x: Base models improve quickly. A fine-tuned model is pinned to its base; when providers retire old models, fine-tunes must be redone.
Plan for change
Often the new base wins
Teams frequently find that a newer base model with a good prompt beats their older fine-tune, letting them drop the fine-tune entirely.
Model deprecation
Cloud providers retire model versions on published schedules, sometimes within a year or two. Build migration into your roadmap.
Prompts, data and evaluations are durable assets; specific model weights are not.

quiz.q: Que faut-il essayer avant d'affiner ?
quiz.explain: Ils coûtent moins cher et suffisent souvent.

quiz.q: Que fait LoRA ?
options: Entraîne de petites matrices additionnelles en gelant le modèle de base
quiz.explain: Un affinage efficace.

quiz.q: Dans la distillation, le petit modèle apprend à partir…
options: Des productions d'un modèle enseignant plus grand
quiz.explain: L'élève imite l'enseignant.

lessons.title: Outils et agents
lessons.summary: Des modèles qui agissent, pas seulement qui répondent.

cards.title: Utilisation d'outils
cards.text: On peut donner des outils à un modèle : des fonctions qu'il peut appeler, comme « search_web », « get_order_status » ou « run_sql ». Il décide quand les appeler et utilise les résultats dans sa réponse.

deep.x: Tool use connects a model to the outside world: databases, search, calculators, business systems and other software. The model chooses which tool to call and with what arguments.

steps: Model answers or calls another tool

deep.x: Why tools matter

items.b: create tickets, send messages, update records

deep.x: Read vs write tools
Read-only tools (search, query) are low risk; write tools (send email, place order, change records) need stronger controls and often human confirmation.
Tool descriptions matter
Clear names, descriptions and parameter definitions help the model use tools correctly. Poor descriptions cause wrong calls.
Tools turn a model from a talker into a doer, which multiplies both usefulness and risk.

cards.title: Comment fonctionne l'appel de fonctions
cards.text: Le développeur décrit chaque outil par un nom, un rôle et des paramètres. Le modèle renvoie une demande structurée ; l'application l'exécute et renvoie le résultat.

deep.x: Function calling is a structured protocol between the application and the model. The model never runs code itself; it requests a call, and your application decides whether to execute it.
Example
Parallel and multi-step calls
Models can request several tools at once (check stock in three warehouses) or chain calls (find customer, then their orders, then shipment status).
Control points
Your application can validate arguments, check permissions, ask the user for confirmation and log every call before executing.
The application, not the model, holds credentials to systems, so access is controlled by your code.

cards.title: Ce qui fait un agent
cards.text: Un agent tourne en boucle : planifier, agir avec des outils, observer les résultats, et continuer jusqu'à atteindre l'objectif ou avoir besoin d'aide.

deep.x: Definitions vary, but an agent generally has a goal, can take multiple actions using tools, observes results and decides next steps with some autonomy.
Components
Autonomy levels

items.b: acts on request in a narrow scope
runs long tasks with minimal oversight

deep.x: Workflows vs agents
Many reliable systems are "workflows" with fixed steps and some model calls, rather than open-ended agents. Use agent autonomy only where flexibility is needed.
Start with the simplest design that works; add autonomy when the task demands it.

cards.title: Agents de code
cards.text: Les agents de code lisent une base de code, modifient des fichiers, lancent des tests et corrigent les erreurs en boucle. C'est l'un des usages d'agents les plus mûrs, car les tests donnent un retour clair.

deep.x: Coding is the most mature agent domain because it offers rich tools (file editing, terminals, tests) and objective feedback (tests pass or fail).
Measured progress
On SWE-bench Verified, a benchmark of real GitHub issues, top systems rose from solving a small fraction in early 2024 to the large majority by 2025.
How developers use them
Good practice

x: Clear task descriptions and acceptance criteria
Sandboxed environments for agents running commands

deep.x: Developers increasingly describe their role shifting from writing every line to specifying, reviewing and steering agent-written code.

cards.title: Utilisation du navigateur et de l'ordinateur
cards.text: Certains agents pilotent des sites web et des applications de bureau en lisant l'écran et en cliquant, ce qui sert quand aucune API n'existe, mais c'est plus lent et plus sujet aux erreurs que les API.

deep.x: Computer-use agents see screenshots and control mouse and keyboard, operating software built for humans. Browser agents navigate websites, fill forms and extract information.
Uses
Challenges

x: Each step is slow compared with an API call
Malicious pages can attempt prompt injection

deep.x: Safety practices
Run in sandboxed browsers or virtual machines, restrict sites, require approval for purchases or submissions, and never give agents unrestricted access to sensitive accounts.
Prefer APIs when available; use computer use as the bridge to systems that have none.

cards.title: Model Context Protocol
cards.text: MCP est un standard ouvert (introduit par Anthropic en 2024) pour connecter les assistants IA à des outils et des sources de données, de sorte qu'un seul connecteur fonctionne avec différentes applications d'IA.

deep.x: MCP, introduced by Anthropic in November 2024 and since adopted widely across the industry, standardises how AI applications connect to tools and data. It's often compared to a USB-C port for AI.
Components

items.b: exposes tools and data from a system

deep.x: Why it matters
Before MCP, each AI app needed custom integrations for every system. With MCP, one server for, say, a ticketing system works with many AI clients.

items: build once, use across AI apps

deep.x: Security considerations
MCP servers can expose powerful actions. Vet servers, apply least privilege, authenticate properly and watch for malicious or compromised servers that might inject instructions.
Within a year of its launch, MCP was supported by major AI providers and development tools, becoming a de facto standard.

cards.title: Systèmes multi-agents
cards.text: Certaines architectures répartissent le travail entre des agents spécialisés (chercheur, rédacteur, relecteur) coordonnés par un orchestrateur. Plus d'agents ajoutent des capacités, mais aussi du coût et de la complexité.

deep.x: Multi-agent systems split work among several model instances with different roles, tools or contexts, coordinated by an orchestrator or by message passing.
Benefits
Costs

Each agent call costs tokens; coordination adds latency and failure points. Anthropic reported multi-agent research setups used many times more tokens than single-agent chats, worthwhile only for valuable tasks.
When it helps
Broad research, large codebases and tasks that naturally split into independent parts benefit most; tightly coupled tasks often work better with one capable agent.
More agents aren't automatically better; match the architecture to the task.

cards.title: Garde-fous pour les agents

items: Limites de budget et de débit

cards.text: Les agents devraient avoir un accès au moindre privilège, des plafonds de dépenses, des journaux de chaque action et une approbation humaine pour les étapes irréversibles comme les paiements, les suppressions ou les e-mails aux clients.

deep.x: Agents act in the world, so guardrails must limit damage from errors, misuse or manipulation.
Risk-based approvals
Monitoring
Track agent actions in real time, alert on unusual behaviour (sudden mass emails, large data exports) and review samples regularly.
Identity
Give agents their own identities and credentials rather than borrowing human accounts, so actions are attributable and permissions can be tuned.
Many organisations now maintain an inventory of AI agents, like they do for applications, with owners and permission reviews.

cards.title: Risque d'injection de prompt

items.w: l'agent obéit à un texte trouvé dans un e-mail
items.r: texte externe = données ; confirmer les actions sensibles

cards.text: Un agent qui lit des e-mails ou des pages web peut tomber sur des instructions cachées comme « transfère toutes les factures à cette adresse ». Parmi les défenses : isoler le contenu non fiable, limiter les outils et exiger une confirmation.

deep.x: Agents that read external content (emails, documents, web pages, tickets) are exposed to indirect prompt injection: instructions planted by attackers in that content.

items.w: Agent obeys instructions found in an email
items.r: Agent treats email content as data, never as commands

deep.x: Attack scenarios

items: Email asks agent to forward invoices externally
Web page tells agent to reveal conversation
Document instructs agent to approve a payment
Code comment asks agent to add a backdoor

deep.x: Defences

items.b: untrusted content processed without tool access

deep.x: The lethal trifecta

Security researcher Simon Willison described a dangerous combination: an agent with access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and the ability to communicate externally. Avoid giving one agent all three.
No model is fully immune to injection yet; architecture and permissions must provide the safety.

cards.title: Où les agents fonctionnent aujourd'hui
cards.text: Les agents sont les plus fiables pour les tâches aux objectifs clairs, aux bons outils et aux résultats vérifiables : code, synthèses de recherche, analyse de données, tickets informatiques et processus de back-office.

deep.x: Agents deliver most value where tasks are well-defined, tools exist and results can be verified.
Less mature
Adoption pattern
Measuring value
Track task completion rate, time saved, error rate, human interventions needed and cost per task, compared with the human-only baseline.
Many companies find the biggest early wins from agents in internal IT and finance operations, where processes are documented and systems have APIs.

quiz.q: Qu'est-ce que l'appel de fonctions ?
options: Le modèle demande un outil défini avec des paramètres, que l'application exécute
Écrire des fonctions à la main
quiz.explain: L'application exécute l'outil demandé par le modèle.

quiz.q: Qu'est-ce qui fait d'un système un « agent » plutôt qu'un chatbot ?
options: Il boucle : planifie, agit avec des outils, observe et continue
quiz.explain: Une action autonome en plusieurs étapes.

quiz.q: De quoi un agent doit-il disposer avant de supprimer des données ou de payer ?
quiz.explain: Les actions irréversibles exigent une supervision.

lessons.title: Évaluer l'IA générative
lessons.summary: Comment savoir si c'est bon ?

cards.title: Pourquoi les évaluations comptent
cards.text: Les sorties génératives varient et les modèles changent. Sans évaluation systématique, vous vous fiez aux impressions de quelques exemples, ce qui peut être très trompeur.

deep.x: Evaluations (evals) turn subjective impressions into measurable evidence. They're essential because generative outputs vary, models update, and small changes can have surprising effects.
What evals enable
The demo trap
Impressive demos use favourable examples. Real users bring messy, varied inputs; only evaluation on representative data reveals true performance.
Evals are the unit tests of AI systems: tedious to build, invaluable once you have them.

cards.title: Construire un jeu de test
cards.text: Rassemblez de vraies entrées de votre cas d'usage, avec des réponses attendues ou des critères clairs. Incluez des cas faciles, difficiles et limites. 50 à 200 exemples bien choisis vont déjà loin.

deep.x: A good test set reflects the real distribution of inputs plus the hard cases that matter most.
Sources

items: Real user queries or documents, anonymised

deep.x: Expected outputs
For each case, define the ideal answer or clear criteria: required facts, forbidden content, format rules.
Keep it growing
Add every production failure to the test set, so the same mistake is caught next time.
Keep part of the test set hidden from people tuning prompts, to avoid unconsciously overfitting to it.

cards.title: Métriques exactes
cards.text: Pour l'extraction et la classification, comparez les sorties aux bonnes réponses : exactitude, précision, rappel, correspondance exacte des champs.

deep.x: When there's a clear right answer, automatic comparison is cheap, fast and objective.
Field-level extraction scoring
Normalisation
Compare normalised values (dates in one format, numbers without separators, trimmed text) so trivial differences don't count as errors.
Confusion matrices
For classification, look at which labels get confused; it reveals ambiguous categories or missing guidance.
Use exact metrics wherever possible; reserve subjective scoring for genuinely open-ended outputs.

cards.title: LLM comme juge
cards.text: Pour du texte libre, un autre modèle peut noter les sorties selon une grille (« Est-ce fidèle à la source ? Le ton est-il juste ? »). Calibrez d'abord le juge sur des notes humaines.

deep.x: An LLM judge scores outputs against a rubric, enabling evaluation of open-ended text at scale. Studies found strong models' judgements correlate well with human ratings on many tasks, but with known biases.
Known biases

items: Self-preference: favours its own model family

deep.x: Making judges reliable

items.b: "Is every claim supported by the source?"

deep.x: Pairwise vs absolute
Asking "which of these two is better?" is often more reliable than scoring each output alone.
Chatbot Arena popularised large-scale pairwise human comparisons of models, producing widely watched leaderboards.

cards.title: Relecture humaine
cards.text: Des experts qui notent un échantillon de sorties restent la référence en matière de qualité, surtout dans les domaines à enjeux élevés. Utilisez des grilles claires pour garder des notes cohérentes.

deep.x: Human experts remain the reference for quality, especially for nuance, domain correctness and high stakes.

items: Blind review: hide which model produced output

deep.x: What humans catch
Cost-effective review
Combine automated metrics and LLM judges for breadth, and human review on samples, disagreements and high-risk outputs.

steps: Humans review samples and flagged items

deep.x: Reviewer fatigue
Long review sessions reduce quality; rotate reviewers and keep sessions short.
Human review time is the scarcest resource; spend it where machines are least reliable.

cards.title: Tests A/B
cards.text: En production, comparez deux versions (prompts ou modèles) sur du trafic réel : notes des utilisateurs, tâches menées à bien, retouches nécessaires, escalades.

deep.x: A/B tests compare variants with real users and real tasks, capturing effects offline evaluation misses: user behaviour, satisfaction and business outcomes.

steps: Variant B: new prompt or model

deep.x: What to measure
Pitfalls

x: Too little traffic for significant results
Novelty effects: users react to change itself
Measuring easy metrics instead of meaningful ones

deep.x: Gradual rollout
Start with a small percentage of traffic, monitor closely, then expand.
Some teams find users prefer slightly shorter answers even when longer ones score higher in offline evaluations.

cards.title: Tests de régression
cards.text: Quand vous changez un prompt ou mettez à niveau un modèle, relancez le jeu d'évaluation pour repérer ce qui s'est dégradé. Traitez les prompts comme du code avec des tests automatisés.

deep.x: A regression is when something that used to work stops working. In GenAI systems, regressions come from prompt edits, model updates, retrieval changes or new data.
Automate it
Run evaluations automatically in the development pipeline, like unit tests, blocking deployment if key metrics fall below thresholds.
Model updates
When providers update a model behind the same name, behaviour can shift. Pin specific versions for critical systems and test before upgrading.
Never assume a "small" prompt tweak is safe; measure it.

cards.title: Mesurer ce qui compte
cards.text: La précision seule ne suffit pas : suivez aussi la latence, le coût par tâche, les incidents de sécurité, la satisfaction des utilisateurs et la fréquence des corrections humaines.

deep.x: A complete picture combines quality, efficiency, safety and user outcomes.

items: Business: time saved, revenue, risk reduced

deep.x: Cost per task
Track total cost per completed task, including retries, tool calls and human corrections, not just price per token.
Human correction rate
How often do people need to edit or override outputs, and how much? It's a direct measure of real-world usefulness.
The best metric is the one closest to the outcome you actually care about.

cards.title: Benchmarks ou votre tâche
cards.text: Les benchmarks publics (MMLU, tests de code) comparent les modèles en général, mais votre tâche peut différer. Un modèle qui gagne les benchmarks n'est pas toujours le meilleur pour vos documents et vos utilisateurs.

deep.x: Public benchmarks test general capabilities, useful for shortlisting models but not for final choices.
Limitations

items: Contamination: test questions leaked into training data

deep.x: Your own benchmark
A private evaluation set built from your documents, languages and tasks is the most reliable guide for your decisions, and can't be contaminated by public training data.
Price-performance
Smaller, cheaper models often reach "good enough" quality on specific tasks; evaluate several tiers.
Benchmark scores for leading models on MMLU went from around 70% in 2022 to around 90% within two years, prompting harder benchmarks.

cards.title: Surveillance en production
cards.text: Journalisez les entrées et sorties (dans le respect de la vie privée), échantillonnez-les pour relecture, surveillez la dérive et recueillez les retours des utilisateurs (pouce haut/bas) pour enrichir votre jeu de test.

deep.x: Production monitoring closes the loop: real usage reveals problems no test set anticipated.
What to monitor
Privacy-aware logging
Log enough to diagnose problems while respecting data protection: mask personal data, restrict access, set retention periods and inform users.
Feedback loops
Make feedback easy (one click) and act on it visibly; users give more feedback when they see it leads to improvements.
Teams that review even 20 real conversations a week typically find issues that metrics alone miss.

quiz.q: Quel est le problème quand on juge un modèle sur quelques exemples ?
options: Les impressions tirées de quelques cas peuvent être très trompeuses
quiz.explain: Il faut des évaluations systématiques.

quiz.q: Avant de faire confiance à un LLM juge, il faut…
options: Vérifier qu'il concorde avec les notes humaines
quiz.explain: Calibrer le juge.

quiz.q: Pourquoi relancer les évaluations lors d'une mise à niveau de modèle ?
options: Pour repérer les régressions où les résultats se sont dégradés
quiz.explain: Les nouveaux modèles peuvent changer de comportement.

lessons.title: Hallucinations et ancrage
lessons.summary: Pourquoi les modèles inventent, et comment limiter cela.

cards.title: Ce qu'est une hallucination
cards.text: Une hallucination est une production fluide et assurée, mais fausse ou sans fondement : citations inventées, chiffres erronés, clauses inexistantes. Elle survient parce que le modèle génère du texte plausible, pas des faits vérifiés.

deep.x: In generative AI, a hallucination is content that's fluent and confident but false, fabricated or unsupported by the provided sources. The term covers invented facts, fake citations, wrong numbers and misread documents.

items: Factual: wrong facts about the world

deep.x: Why it happens

x: The training objective rewards plausible continuations, not verified truth
Evaluation and training have historically rewarded guessing over abstaining
Rare facts are weakly encoded and easily blended with similar ones
Models are pushed to be helpful and complete

deep.x: A 2025 view

OpenAI researchers argued in 2025 that hallucinations persist partly because benchmarks score a confident guess better than "I don't know", so models learn to guess. Rewarding calibrated abstention could reduce it.
Hallucination isn't lying: the model has no intent; it's producing likely text without a built-in truth check.

cards.title: Quand c'est le plus probable
cards.text: Les hallucinations augmentent avec les sujets obscurs, les chiffres et dates exacts, les longues listes, les demandes de citations, les événements récents postérieurs à la date limite, et les questions aux prémisses fausses.

deep.x: Risk depends on the question type, the domain and whether the model has sources.
High-risk patterns
False premises
"Why did Portugal win the 1966 World Cup?" may elicit an invented explanation instead of a correction (Portugal finished third). Good models now challenge false premises more often, but not always.

items.r: Correcting it: "Portugal didn't win, it finished third in 1966"

deep.x: Long outputs
Errors accumulate over long lists and documents; spot-check the middle and end, not just the start.
Asking for "10 examples" of something rare can push a model to invent the last few to meet the number.

cards.title: Ancrage
cards.text: Donnez au modèle le matériau source et demandez-lui de ne répondre qu'à partir de celui-ci. Les réponses ancrées hallucinent bien moins et peuvent être vérifiées.

deep.x: Grounding ties answers to authoritative sources supplied at question time: documents, database results or search results. The model's job shifts from recalling to reading and synthesising.
Grounding instructions

items: "If the answer isn't there, say so"

deep.x: Measuring faithfulness
Faithfulness checks whether every claim in the answer is supported by the sources. Automated checkers and human reviews can measure the rate of unsupported claims.
Limits
Grounded systems can still misread sources, mix up similar documents or over-generalise. Retrieval errors also undermine grounding.
Grounding doesn't eliminate errors, but it makes them findable.

cards.title: Autoriser le « je ne sais pas »

items.r: « réponds d'après les documents ; sinon, dis-le »

cards.text: Dites explicitement au modèle qu'il peut répondre qu'il ne sait pas ou que la réponse ne figure pas dans les documents. Sinon, il peut se sentir poussé à produire quelque chose.

deep.x: Models trained to be helpful may feel pressure to answer everything. Explicit permission and instructions to abstain reduce fabrication.

items.r: "Answer the question, if the information isn't available, say 'Not found' and explain what's missing"

deep.x: Calibration
A calibrated system is confident when right and uncertain when unsure. Asking the model to rate its confidence, or to separate "known from source" vs "inferred", helps users judge reliability.
Product design
Interfaces that show "No answer found in your documents" with suggestions for where to look build more trust than confident guesses.
In evaluations, systems that abstain appropriately often score lower on "accuracy" metrics that count abstentions as wrong, another reason to choose metrics carefully.

cards.title: Citations et extraits
cards.text: Demandez des extraits ou des citations pour chaque affirmation. Puis vérifiez un échantillon : les modèles peuvent aussi inventer des citations, alors contrôlez que le texte cité existe vraiment.

deep.x: Citations help users verify claims. Exact quotes are even better because they can be matched against the source automatically.
Verify citations exist

Models can generate citations that look real but aren't: fake paper titles, wrong page numbers or quotes that don't appear in the source. Automated string matching against retrieved text catches many of these.
Good citation design

items: Link to document and page or section
Show the quoted text on hover or click
Cite after each claim, not only at the end

deep.x: For research
When using AI to find academic sources, always check the papers exist and say what's claimed. Use dedicated research tools connected to real databases.
Courts and academic journals have rejected submissions after finding AI-fabricated references.

cards.title: Des outils pour les faits
cards.text: Pour les calculs, utilisez un outil de code ou une calculatrice. Pour les données en direct, utilisez la recherche ou une API. Laissez le modèle orchestrer et expliquer, pas mémoriser.

deep.x: Language models are poor calculators and unreliable databases. Tools let them delegate those jobs to systems built for accuracy.
Example
Code interpreters
Assistants that run code in a sandbox can analyse spreadsheets, compute statistics and draw charts with exact results, then explain them in plain language.
Orchestration
The model's role becomes understanding the request, choosing the right tools, combining results and communicating them clearly.
Let models do language and reasoning; let tools do facts and arithmetic.

cards.title: Le raisonnement aide, en partie
cards.text: Le raisonnement pas à pas et l'auto-vérification réduisent certaines erreurs, surtout en logique et en maths, mais n'éliminent pas les hallucinations factuelles.

deep.x: Reasoning reduces errors from careless logic and arithmetic slips, and lets models check their work. But reasoning can't create knowledge the model doesn't have.
Mixed findings

Some evaluations found reasoning models hallucinated more on certain factual questions, possibly because longer generations give more opportunities for invented details. Results vary by model and task.
Combine reasoning with tools
Self-verification
Prompting the model to list claims and check each one against sources ("chain of verification") reduced hallucinations in research studies.
Reasoning traces can contain errors that the final answer quietly corrects, or vice versa, so check the final answer, not just the reasoning.

cards.title: Concevoir pour la vérification
cards.text: Pour les usages à enjeux élevés, concevez le processus de sorte qu'un humain vérifie les faits clés avant leur utilisation : mettez en évidence les valeurs extraites à côté de la source, signalez les faibles niveaux de confiance.

deep.x: The best defence against hallucination is a workflow where checking is easy and expected.

steps: Shows each next to its source

deep.x: UI patterns
Risk-based review
Measuring the process
Track how often humans correct AI outputs and which fields are corrected most; use this to improve prompts, data or models, and to set thresholds.
Make the right action the easy action: verification should take seconds, not minutes.

cards.title: Conséquences réelles

items.w: citer des affaires suggérées par l'IA
items.r: vérifier chaque affaire dans une base officielle

cards.text: Des avocats aux États-Unis et ailleurs ont été sanctionnés pour avoir déposé des mémoires judiciaires contenant des jurisprudences inventées par l'IA. Vérifiez toujours avant de vous appuyer sur une production de l'IA dans un cadre professionnel.

deep.x: In 2023, in *Mata v. Avianca*, US lawyers submitted a brief citing six non-existent cases generated by ChatGPT and were fined $5,000. Similar incidents followed in the US, UK, Canada and elsewhere, including cases where judges' or experts' filings contained AI errors.
Other domains

items.b: an airline chatbot invented a refund policy

deep.x: The Air Canada case
In 2024 a Canadian tribunal held Air Canada liable for its chatbot's incorrect promise of a bereavement fare refund, rejecting the argument that the chatbot was a separate entity.
Lessons
Organisations are accountable for what their AI systems say and do. Professionals remain responsible for work they submit, however it was drafted.
Many courts now require lawyers to disclose AI use or certify that citations have been checked.

cards.title: L'hallucination recule, sans être résolue

items: Plus faible : ancré dans des sources
Maximal : faits de niche non ancrés

cards.text: Les modèles récents hallucinent moins, et l'ancrage associé aux outils les réduit encore, mais aucun modèle actuel n'en est exempt. Considérez la production de l'IA comme un bon brouillon, pas comme un fait vérifié.

deep.x: Successive model generations have reduced hallucination rates on many benchmarks, and grounding, tools and better training help further. But no model is hallucination-free, and rates vary widely by task.
Industry tracking
Leaderboards measuring hallucination in summarisation tasks show leading models' rates falling to low single-digit percentages, but rates on open-ended factual questions remain much higher.

v.unit: hallucination rate in document summaries, % (illustrative trend)

deep.x: Realistic expectations
Use AI like a very fast, well-read junior colleague: valuable drafts, checked before they matter.

quiz.q: Pourquoi les LLM hallucinent-ils ?
options: Ils génèrent du texte plausible plutôt que des faits vérifiés
quiz.explain: Fluidité ne veut pas dire vérité.

quiz.q: Quelle consigne réduit les hallucinations dans des questions-réponses sur documents ?
options: « Réponds uniquement à partir des documents ; dis-le si ce n'est pas dedans »
quiz.explain: L'ancrage, plus la permission de dire « je ne sais pas ».

quiz.q: Comment traiter les calculs exacts ?
options: Utiliser un outil de code ou une calculatrice
quiz.explain: Les outils sont fiables pour l'arithmétique.

lessons.title: Contexte, mémoire et longs documents
lessons.summary: Ce que le modèle peut voir, et pendant combien de temps.

cards.title: La fenêtre de contexte
cards.text: Tout ce que le modèle considère à la fois (prompt système, conversation, documents, résultats d'outils) doit tenir dans sa fenêtre de contexte, mesurée en tokens. Les fenêtres actuelles vont de dizaines de milliers à plus d'un million de tokens.

deep.x: The context window is the total number of tokens the model can process in one request: input plus output. It's the model's working memory for that request.
Sizes today
Input vs output limits
Models also have a maximum output length, often much smaller than the context window. Long reports may need to be generated in sections.
What counts
Everything counts: system prompt, earlier messages, attached files, tool results and the answer itself. Long chats fill the window quickly.
An image attached to a chat may consume around a thousand tokens or more, depending on resolution and the model.

cards.title: Plus grand n'est pas toujours mieux
cards.text: Les contextes très longs coûtent plus cher, prennent plus de temps, et les modèles peuvent manquer des détails enfouis au milieu. Ne récupérer que les parties pertinentes donne souvent des réponses meilleures et moins chères.

deep.x: Long context is convenient but has costs. Price, latency and sometimes accuracy suffer as context grows.
Cost scaling
Accuracy effects
Benchmarks like "needle in a haystack" show modern models can find a single planted fact in long contexts, but harder tasks, reasoning over many scattered facts, degrade with length.
When long context shines

items: Analysing one long contract end to end

deep.x: Use long context for genuinely holistic tasks; use retrieval for lookups.

cards.title: Perdu au milieu
cards.text: Des études montrent que les modèles retiennent mieux l'information au début et à la fin des longs contextes qu'au milieu. Placez les instructions clés et la question vers la fin, après les longs documents.

deep.x: A 2023 Stanford study, "Lost in the Middle", found models used information at the beginning and end of long inputs much better than information in the middle: a U-shaped curve.

v.unit: accuracy by position of key information, % (illustrative)

deep.x: Practical tips

items: Put instructions and the question at the end
Repeat key constraints near the end
Use headings and labels in long inputs

deep.x: Newer models
Training on long-context tasks has reduced, but not eliminated, the effect in newer models. Test with your own documents.
Order matters in RAG too
When inserting retrieved passages, put the most relevant ones where the model attends best, often at the start and end.
Humans show a similar serial-position effect: we remember the first and last items in a list best.

cards.title: Mémoire de conversation
cards.text: Les applications de chat renvoient les messages précédents au modèle à chaque tour. Quand une conversation devient très longue, les parties anciennes sont résumées ou abandonnées : des détails du début peuvent donc être oubliés.

deep.x: Language models are stateless: they don't remember previous requests. Chat apps simulate memory by resending the conversation history with each new message.
Managing long chats
Symptoms of overflow
The model forgets early instructions, contradicts earlier decisions or loses details from documents attached at the start.
Tip
For long projects, keep a running summary of key decisions and paste it into new chats, or use project features that store reference documents.
If an assistant "forgets" something you said, it may simply have scrolled out of its context.

cards.title: Mémoire à long terme
cards.text: Certains assistants enregistrent des faits d'une conversation à l'autre, comme vos préférences ou vos projets, et les retrouvent plus tard. Vous devriez pouvoir consulter et supprimer ce qui est mémorisé.

deep.x: Memory features let assistants persist information across conversations, like your role, preferences or ongoing projects, and bring it back when relevant.
Types

items.b: files agents write for later steps

deep.x: Control and privacy
Benefits and risks
Agent systems often keep "scratchpad" notes in files to remember progress across long tasks that exceed one context window.

cards.title: Mise en cache de prompt
cards.text: Si de nombreuses requêtes partagent le même long préfixe (instructions, gros document), les fournisseurs peuvent le mettre en cache, ce qui réduit coût et latence pour les appels répétés.

deep.x: Prompt caching stores the processed state of a repeated prompt prefix, such as long system instructions or a large document. Subsequent requests reusing that prefix skip recomputation.

v.unit: relative cost of cached input tokens (typical)

deep.x: How to benefit

items: Put stable content first: instructions, documents
Put variable content last: the user's question
Reuse the same prefix across many requests

deep.x: Savings
Providers often discount cached tokens by around 90%, and latency drops noticeably for long prompts.

steps: Request 2: reuse cache, process only new part

deep.x: Use cases

x: Q&A over the same long document

deep.x: Structure prompts with the unchanging parts first to unlock caching.

cards.title: Résumer et map-reduce
cards.text: Pour les documents trop longs pour un seul appel, résumez les sections séparément puis combinez les résumés : un schéma « map-reduce ».

deep.x: When content exceeds the context window, or a single pass gives shallow results, split the work: process pieces independently (map), then combine the outputs (reduce).
Variations

items.b: iterate through parts, updating a running summary
pull facts from each part, then analyse together

deep.x: Pitfalls

x: Consistent formats needed for clean merging

deep.x: Example
Summarising 200 supplier contracts: extract key terms from each (map), then aggregate into a comparison table and risk summary (reduce).
Map steps can run in parallel, so processing hundreds of documents takes minutes rather than hours.

cards.title: Ingénierie du contexte
cards.text: Construire de bonnes applications d'IA consiste en grande partie à décider de ce qui entre dans le contexte : quelles instructions, quels passages récupérés, quelles sorties d'outils, dans quel ordre et quel format.

deep.x: Context engineering is the discipline of deciding exactly what information the model sees, in what form and order. It has largely replaced "prompt engineering" as the central skill in building AI applications.
Principles
For agents
Agents accumulate tool outputs and history over many steps. Techniques like summarising old steps, pruning irrelevant results and writing notes to files keep context focused.
Failure modes
Most "model failures" in applications are really context failures: the model didn't see what it needed.

cards.title: Budgets de tokens

items.w: coller tout le manuel de 200 pages à chaque fois
items.r: récupérer les 3 sections pertinentes

cards.text: Chaque token en entrée coûte de l'argent et du temps. Supprimez le texte superflu, dédoublonnez les passages récupérés et gardez des instructions concises sans perdre en clarté.

deep.x: Tokens cost money and time. Efficient context design reduces costs without hurting quality.
Savings levers

items: Use smaller models for simple steps

deep.x: Output tokens
Output tokens often cost several times more than input tokens; asking for concise answers or structured outputs saves money.
Balance
Don't over-trim: cutting essential context to save tokens can cost more in errors and rework. Measure quality alongside cost.
Optimise tokens like any other cloud resource: measure, then trim what doesn't add value.

cards.title: Confidentialité dans le contexte
cards.text: Tout ce que vous mettez dans le contexte est envoyé au fournisseur du modèle. Vérifiez les règles de votre organisation sur les données personnelles et confidentielles, et utilisez les outils d'entreprise approuvés.

deep.x: Anything placed in a model's context is processed by the model provider's systems. Data protection rules and company policies apply.
Enterprise safeguards
Shadow AI
Employees pasting sensitive data into personal accounts of consumer AI tools is a major risk. Providing approved, easy-to-use tools reduces it.
Minimise
Only include data needed for the task; mask or pseudonymise personal identifiers where possible.
Surveys in 2024–25 found a large share of employees using AI tools at work that their employers hadn't approved.

quiz.q: Où placer la question clé dans un long prompt ?
options: Vers la fin, après les longs documents
quiz.explain: Les modèles portent bien leur attention sur la fin.

quiz.q: Qu'économise la mise en cache de prompt ?
options: Du coût et de la latence pour des préfixes longs répétés
quiz.explain: Les préfixes réutilisés sont mis en cache.

quiz.q: Comment résumer un document trop long pour la fenêtre de contexte ?
options: Résumer les sections, puis combiner les résumés
quiz.explain: Le résumé en map-reduce.

lessons.title: Le paysage des modèles
lessons.summary: Fermés, ouverts et comment choisir.

cards.title: Les laboratoires de pointe
cards.text: Une poignée d'entreprises entraînent les modèles les plus performants, dont OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini) et Meta (Llama), avec une forte concurrence de laboratoires comme Mistral, DeepSeek, Alibaba (Qwen) et xAI.

deep.x: The frontier is defined by the most capable general models. A small number of well-funded labs compete closely, with leadership shifting between them on different capabilities.
Competition dynamics
Leads tend to be short: capabilities first seen in one lab's model often appear in competitors' within months, and open-weight models typically trail the frontier by around a year or less.
Investment
Frontier labs raise and spend tens of billions on compute, data and talent; big tech companies invest hundreds of billions in AI data centres.
Regional players

x: China: DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot, Zhipu and others
Many countries building sovereign models for language and data control

deep.x: For buyers, competition is good news: prices fall and quality rises quickly.

cards.title: Poids fermés ou ouverts

items: hébergement et sécurité à votre charge

cards.text: Les modèles fermés s'utilisent via une API ; le fournisseur les héberge et les met à jour. Les modèles à poids ouverts peuvent être téléchargés, exécutés en privé et affinés, mais vous les exploitez vous-même.

deep.x: "Open-weight" models release their parameters for download; "closed" models are accessible only via the provider's API or apps.
Spectrum of openness

items.b: weights, code, often data and training details

deep.x: Enterprise considerations
Hybrid strategies
Many organisations combine both: closed models for complex tasks, open models on-premise for sensitive or high-volume tasks, behind a common gateway.
The Open Source Initiative published a formal definition of "open source AI" in 2024, stricter than most "open-weight" releases.

cards.title: Tailles et gammes de modèles

items: Grand : tâches ardues, plus lent, coûteux

cards.text: Les fournisseurs proposent généralement des gammes : grands modèles pour le raisonnement difficile, moyens pour la plupart des tâches, petits et rapides pour les travaux simples à fort volume. Choisir le plus petit modèle qui fait le travail permet de grosses économies.

deep.x: Providers offer model families in several sizes. Larger models are more capable but slower and pricier; smaller ones are fast and cheap.
Price differences
Right-sizing
Speed matters too
For interactive use, latency affects user experience; small models can respond almost instantly.
Many production systems use several tiers at once, routed by task difficulty.

cards.title: Choisir un modèle
cards.text: Testez des candidats sur vos propres tâches. Prenez en compte la qualité, la vitesse, le coût, la longueur de contexte, la résidence des données, les conditions de confidentialité et l'adéquation du fournisseur avec votre cloud.

deep.x: Model selection should be driven by evaluation on your own tasks, not headlines or general benchmarks.
Evaluation process
Avoid lock-in
Re-evaluate regularly
With new releases every few months, revisit choices at least twice a year.
Teams often find that the "best" model differs by task: one excels at extraction, another at writing, another at code.

cards.title: Accès en entreprise
cards.text: Les grandes entreprises utilisent souvent les modèles via leur cloud : Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock ou Google Vertex AI, qui offrent sécurité d'entreprise, hébergement régional et contrats.

deep.x: Large organisations usually access models through cloud platforms that add enterprise security, compliance and integration.

items.b: OpenAI and other models in Microsoft's cloud

deep.x: What enterprises get
Integration benefits
Using your existing cloud simplifies security reviews, billing, networking and connecting AI to data already hosted there.
Capacity
High-volume users may need reserved or provisioned throughput to guarantee capacity and latency during peaks.
For companies standardised on one cloud, its AI platform is usually the path of least resistance, though multi-cloud access widens model choice.

cards.title: Routage de modèles
cards.text: Au lieu d'un seul modèle pour tout, un routeur envoie chaque requête au modèle le plus adapté : petit pour les requêtes simples, grand pour les complexes. Une passerelle IA peut gérer le routage, la journalisation et les quotas.

deep.x: Routing sends each request to the most appropriate model based on difficulty, cost, latency or data sensitivity.
Routing signals
AI gateways
An AI gateway sits between applications and models, providing routing, authentication, rate limits, cost tracking, logging, caching and fallback when a provider fails.

items: AI gateway: routing, keys, logs, quotas

deep.x: Savings
Routing most traffic to cheaper models while reserving premium models for hard cases can cut costs substantially without lowering quality, if the router is evaluated well.
Gateways also let organisations switch providers quickly during outages or when a better model appears.

cards.title: Un domaine en évolution rapide

items: Abstraire le modèle derrière une interface

cards.text: De nouveaux modèles apparaissent tous les quelques mois, égalant souvent le meilleur de l'an dernier pour une fraction du prix. Concevez vos systèmes pour pouvoir changer de modèle sans tout réécrire.

deep.x: Model capabilities and prices change rapidly. Capability that cost a fortune one year can be cheap the next.
Architectural implications

items: Avoid deep coupling to one provider's features

deep.x: Deprecations
Providers retire older models on schedules; applications pinned to specific versions must migrate.
Strategy
Build durable assets, such as clean data, evaluation sets, integrations and user workflows, rather than betting on a particular model.
Assume the model you use today will be replaced within a year.

cards.title: Les licences comptent
cards.text: Les modèles à poids ouverts viennent avec des licences différentes : certaines totalement ouvertes (Apache 2,0, MIT), d'autres avec des restrictions d'usage ou des limites pour les très grandes entreprises. Vérifiez avant tout usage commercial.

deep.x: Open-weight models come with licences that determine commercial use, modification and redistribution rights.

items.b: custom terms, restrictions for very large companies

deep.x: What to check
Outputs and derivatives
Some licences extend terms to fine-tuned derivatives; using outputs to improve competing models may be restricted.
Governance
Maintain a register of models in use, their licences and approved purposes, as with open-source software.
Some open-weight licences prohibit use by companies above a certain number of monthly users without a separate agreement.

cards.title: Benchmarks et classements
cards.text: Les classements publics comparent les modèles sur des tests et des votes de préférence humaine. Ce sont des indices utiles, mais ils peuvent être truqués ou ne pas correspondre à votre cas d'usage.

deep.x: Leaderboards aggregate benchmark scores or human preference votes to rank models. They're useful for orientation, but have limits.
Caveats

items: Contamination: test data seen in training
Style bias: preference for longer or friendlier answers

deep.x: Reading leaderboards
Treat leaderboards like restaurant rankings: a guide to what to try, not a substitute for tasting.

cards.title: Coût total de possession
cards.text: Les coûts d'API augmentent avec l'usage ; l'auto-hébergement a des coûts fixes de GPU, d'ingénierie et d'exploitation. À volume faible ou variable, les API sont généralement moins chères ; à très fort volume stable, l'auto-hébergement peut l'emporter.

deep.x: Total cost of ownership (TCO) includes far more than per-token prices.

items: Model usage: tokens or GPU hours

deep.x: API vs self-hosting

items: can be cheaper at steady high volume

deep.x: Utilisation is key
Self-hosted GPUs are only cost-effective if well utilised. Idle GPUs at night or weekends raise effective cost per token.
Hidden costs

x: Prompt and pipeline maintenance as models change

deep.x: For many enterprise use cases, people costs for integration and change management exceed model usage costs.

quiz.q: Quel est un avantage des modèles à poids ouverts ?
options: On peut les exécuter en privé et les personnaliser
quiz.explain: Vous maîtrisez le déploiement.

quiz.q: Que fait un routeur de modèles ?
options: Il envoie chaque requête au modèle le plus adapté
quiz.explain: Il associe les tâches aux modèles.

quiz.q: Comment choisir un modèle ?
options: Tester des candidats sur vos propres tâches et contraintes
quiz.explain: Vos évaluations tranchent.

lessons.title: Exécuter des modèles en local
lessons.summary: L'IA sur votre propre portable ou serveur.

cards.title: Pourquoi exécuter en local ?
cards.text: Confidentialité (rien ne quitte votre machine), usage hors ligne, aucun coût par token et contrôle total. La contrepartie : les modèles locaux sont plus petits et généralement moins performants que les modèles cloud de pointe.

deep.x: Running models on your own hardware gives control over data, cost and availability, at the cost of capability and maintenance.
Good reasons

items: Sensitive documents that can't leave your machine

deep.x: Typical hardware
The capability gap
Open models have narrowed the gap with frontier models, but the largest closed models still lead on complex reasoning and agentic tasks.
Local AI is ideal for privacy-first, focused tasks; frontier cloud models remain best for the hardest problems.

cards.title: Outils
cards.text: Ollama et LM Studio facilitent le téléchargement et la discussion avec des modèles ouverts. llama.cpp exécute efficacement les modèles sur CPU et Apple Silicon ; vLLM sert des modèles à grande échelle sur GPU.

deep.x: A rich ecosystem makes running local models straightforward.

items.b: command-line and API, simple model management
desktop app with chat and model browser
efficient C++ engine for CPUs and GPUs

deep.x: Typical workflow

steps: Chat or call the local API

deep.x: Interfaces

x: Open WebUI: a ChatGPT-like interface for local models
IDE plugins for local coding assistants
Home Assistant integrations for voice and automation

deep.x: Model sources
Hugging Face hosts most open models, with community-quantised versions in GGUF and other formats.
Ollama's model library lets you run a model with a single command like "ollama run llama3", downloading it automatically.

cards.title: La mémoire est la limite
cards.text: Les poids du modèle doivent tenir en RAM ou en mémoire GPU. En quantification 4 bits, un modèle de 7 à 8 Md de paramètres demande environ 4 à 5 Go ; un modèle de 70 Md environ 40 Go.

deep.x: Model weights must fit in memory, plus space for the KV cache that grows with context length.
Rules of thumb
Unified memory advantage
Apple Silicon Macs share memory between CPU and GPU, so a 64 GB Mac can hold models a 24 GB GPU can't, though GPUs are usually faster per token.
Context costs memory
Long contexts need large KV caches; a model that fits with a 4k context might not fit with 64k.
Mixture-of-experts models need memory for all experts but compute for only a few, so they can run surprisingly fast if they fit.

cards.title: Formats de quantification
cards.text: Les fichiers GGUF (pour llama.cpp, Ollama) stockent des poids quantifiés comme Q4_K_M ou Q8_0. Moins de bits, c'est plus petit et plus rapide, avec une certaine perte de qualité.

deep.x: Quantisation formats define how weights are compressed. GGUF, used by llama.cpp and Ollama, is the most common for local use.
Choosing
Other formats

items: EXL2: flexible bit rates for GPUs

deep.x: Trade-off
Choose the largest model that fits at Q4–Q5 rather than a smaller model at Q8: bigger models usually lose less from quantisation.
The "K_M" variants use mixed precision, keeping sensitive layers at higher bits.

cards.title: Vitesse
cards.text: La vitesse se mesure en tokens par seconde. Les Mac Apple Silicon dotés de beaucoup de mémoire unifiée et les PC équipés de gros GPU font tourner confortablement des modèles de taille moyenne.

deep.x: Local generation speed depends mainly on memory bandwidth: each token requires reading the active weights. Prompt processing depends more on compute.
What's usable?
Speed-ups
Batch vs interactive
For overnight batch jobs (classifying thousands of emails), slower speeds are fine; for chat and coding, speed matters more.
Reading speed is about 4–5 words per second, so ~10 tokens per second already feels like a fast typist.

cards.title: API locale

steps: Réponse, rien ne sort de la machine

cards.text: Ollama et les outils similaires exposent une API compatible OpenAI sur votre machine, de sorte que applications et scripts peuvent passer facilement d'un modèle local à un modèle cloud.

deep.x: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM can expose an HTTP API compatible with OpenAI's API format, so existing tools work with local models by changing the base URL.
Benefits

items: Switch between cloud and local by configuration

deep.x: Example

x: Same chat request format as cloud APIs

deep.x: Feature gaps
Not every feature matches cloud APIs exactly: tool calling, structured outputs and vision support vary by model and server. Test what you need.
An OpenAI-compatible local endpoint makes local models a drop-in option for many apps.

cards.title: RAG local
cards.text: Combinez un modèle d'embedding local, une base vectorielle locale et un LLM local pour discuter avec des documents privés entièrement hors ligne.

deep.x: A fully local RAG stack keeps documents, embeddings and generation on your machine.
Components

items.b: small open models, e.g. nomic-embed or bge

deep.x: Use cases
Quality tips

x: Good parsing of PDFs and scans matters most
Choose an embedding model that handles your languages
Smaller local LLMs benefit from fewer, highly relevant passages

deep.x: Open WebUI includes built-in document upload and RAG, giving a private "chat with your files" in minutes.

cards.title: IA de homelab
cards.text: Les homelabs font tourner des modèles locaux à côté de la domotique : résumer des événements de caméra, assistants vocaux dans Home Assistant ou classement de notifications, le tout sans cloud.

deep.x: Homelabs combine local AI with home automation, cameras and media, keeping data private and working without internet.

items.b: local LLM for summaries and commands

deep.x: Example automations

items: Summarise overnight camera events in a morning message
Voice control of lights and climate offline

deep.x: Architecture
Hardware

x: Mini PC with a Coral or small GPU for detection
Separate GPU box or Mac for LLMs

deep.x: Home Assistant's "Assist" can use a local LLM to understand flexible commands like "make it cosier in the living room".

cards.title: Bons cas d'usage en local
cards.text: Le résumé, la classification, l'extraction, la rédaction et l'aide au code fonctionnent bien avec des modèles locaux de taille moyenne. Le raisonnement complexe ou les très longs documents peuvent encore exiger un modèle de pointe.

deep.x: Local models handle many everyday tasks well, especially focused ones with clear inputs.
Matching tasks to models
Hybrid approach
Use local models for private preprocessing (redacting personal data, classifying documents) and send only safe, minimal information to cloud models when needed.
Test local models on your actual tasks; many are better than expected.

cards.title: La sécurité compte toujours
cards.text: Local ne veut pas dire automatiquement sûr : les modèles et outils téléchargés sont des logiciels. Utilisez des sources fiables, gardez l'API hors de l'internet public et mettez à jour régulièrement.

deep.x: Local AI reduces data exposure to providers but introduces its own security responsibilities.

items: Prefer safe formats like GGUF or safetensors
Don't expose local APIs to the internet

deep.x: Model file risks
Older formats based on Python's pickle can execute code when loaded. Safer formats like safetensors and GGUF store only data.

items: safetensors or GGUF from trusted publishers

deep.x: Exposed servers
Security researchers have found thousands of local AI servers accidentally exposed to the internet without authentication, letting anyone use or probe them.
Agents at home
Local agents connected to home automation, files or email still face prompt injection and mistakes; apply the same guardrails as in business.
Default local AI server ports are often scanned by bots; bind services to localhost or protect them behind authentication.

quiz.q: De combien de mémoire un modèle 8B a-t-il besoin en 4 bits ?
quiz.explain: Environ 0,5 octet par paramètre, plus une marge.

quiz.q: Quel est le principal avantage des modèles locaux ?
options: Confidentialité, usage hors ligne et aucun coût par token
quiz.explain: Les données restent sur votre machine.

quiz.q: Quel outil facilite l'exécution locale de modèles ouverts ?
quiz.explain: Une CLI simple et une API locale.

lessons.title: Coût et vitesse
lessons.summary: Tokens, latence et comment rendre l'IA abordable à grande échelle.

cards.title: Tarification au token

viz.f: coût = tokens ent. × prix ent. + tokens sort. × prix sort.

cards.text: Les API facturent par million de tokens d'entrée et de sortie. Les tokens de sortie coûtent généralement plusieurs fois plus que ceux d'entrée, et les grands modèles coûtent bien plus que les petits.

deep.x: Model APIs price usage per million tokens, with separate rates for input and output. Prices vary by model tier, provider, region and features like caching or batch processing.

v.f: cost = input tokens × input price + output tokens × output price

deep.x: Why output costs more
Input tokens are processed in parallel in one pass; output tokens are generated one at a time, each requiring a full pass through the model, so they use more compute per token.
Price tiers

v.unit: price per million output tokens, $ (illustrative tiers)

deep.x: Other charges
Many providers offer free tiers or credits for experimentation, but production use needs proper budgeting.

cards.title: Un exemple chiffré
cards.text: 10 000 requêtes par jour, chacune avec 2 000 tokens d'entrée et 300 de sortie. À 3 $ par million de tokens d'entrée et 15 $ par million de tokens de sortie : 60 $ + 45 $ = 105 $ par jour.

deep.x: Estimating costs early avoids surprises. Start from volumes and token counts per request.
Sensitivity
Hidden multipliers

x: Retries after errors or validation failures
Agent loops calling the model many times per task

deep.x: Budget controls
Always estimate at expected peak volume, not pilot volume.

cards.title: Latence
cards.text: Les utilisateurs ressentent deux délais : le temps avant le premier token (combien de temps avant que le texte commence) et la vitesse de génération (tokens par seconde). Diffuser la réponse en streaming rend l'attente plus courte.

deep.x: Two latency measures shape user experience: time to first token (TTFT), and output speed in tokens per second.
What drives latency
Example

x: Total ≈ 5.5 s, but text appears after 0.5 s

deep.x: Reducing latency
Reasoning models
Thinking time can add seconds to minutes before an answer starts. Show progress indicators or use them asynchronously.
Users perceive streamed answers as faster even when total time is the same, because they can start reading immediately.

cards.title: Le plus petit modèle suffisant
cards.text: Les petits modèles peuvent coûter de 10 à 50 fois moins que les plus grands. Confiez-leur les tâches simples et réservez les gros modèles aux cas difficiles.

deep.x: The cheapest model that meets quality requirements should handle each task. Many tasks don't need frontier intelligence.
Task fit
Cascades
A cascade tries a cheap model first and escalates to a larger one only if confidence is low or validation fails.
Distillation
For very high-volume tasks, fine-tuning a small model on a large model's outputs can deliver large-model quality at small-model prices.
Measure quality per tier on your eval set; the cheapest acceptable tier usually wins.

cards.title: Raccourcir le prompt

items: Mettre en cache les préfixes communs

cards.text: Élaguez les instructions, récupérez moins de passages mais de meilleure qualité et évitez de renvoyer un contexte inchangé. Chaque token économisé l'est à chaque requête.

deep.x: Input tokens are multiplied by every request. Small savings per request add up at scale.
Example savings
Don't cut clarity
Removing context the model needs causes errors and retries that cost more. Test quality after trimming.
Structured outputs save tokens
Asking for JSON with defined fields avoids verbose prose when software is the consumer.
Tool and function definitions count as input tokens on every call; agents with dozens of tools carry a hidden token overhead.

cards.title: Mise en cache

steps: Oui : renvoyer la réponse en cache

cards.text: Mettez en cache les prompts répétés (cache de prompt) et les réponses répétées (cache de réponses). Les questions de type FAQ peuvent souvent être servies depuis un cache.

deep.x: Two kinds of caching cut cost and latency: prompt caching at the provider and response caching in your application.

items: reuses whole answers to identical or similar questions

deep.x: Prompt caching
Put stable content (instructions, reference documents, tool definitions) at the start of prompts. Providers cache it for minutes to hours and charge a fraction for reuse.
Response caching
For FAQs or repeated queries, store answers and serve them directly. Semantic caching matches questions with similar meaning using embeddings.
Cautions

items: Expire cached answers when sources change
Don't cache personalised or sensitive answers inappropriately

deep.x: Caching is often the single biggest cost lever for high-traffic assistants.

cards.title: Traitement par lots
cards.text: Pour le travail non urgent, comme classer pendant la nuit un arriéré de documents, les API par lots offrent de gros rabais (souvent environ moitié prix) en échange d'un délai plus long.

deep.x: Batch APIs process large sets of requests asynchronously, typically within 24 hours, at roughly half the normal price.
Good candidates
Workflow
Combining discounts
Batch processing can combine with prompt caching for further savings on repetitive workloads.
Overnight batch jobs let teams process years of archived documents for a modest one-off cost.

cards.title: Coût du raisonnement
cards.text: Les modèles de raisonnement génèrent de nombreux tokens de « réflexion » avant de répondre. Ils sont plus précis sur les tâches difficiles mais plus lents et plus chers : employez-les là où la qualité supplémentaire compte.

deep.x: Reasoning models generate hidden "thinking" tokens before the visible answer, billed as output tokens. A short visible answer might involve thousands of reasoning tokens.
